bull_bear.body: Reinvesting margin gains into growth (retail expansion, tech, AI); completed full acquisition of Earth Rhythm; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; prioritizing ROCE (now 21.2%) over aggressive capex
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global inflationary pressures (oil, currency) may impact discretionary spending; competitive intensity in D2C beauty/fashion; execution risk in scaling new brands and international ventures
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; emphasized AI-driven efficiency, brand partnerships as moats, and sustainable profitability over pure growth; cautious on macro but optimistic on category resilience (small luxuries)
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Nykaa now manages Nike.com and app in India end-to-end — a rare D2C tech services partnership; Superstore’s 30% self-serve orders indicate deep retailer stickiness; House of Nykaa brands are now distributed via 150,000+ GT doors — a hidden offline retail footprint
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital efficiency framed as the core narrative: ROCE (annualised for Q1FY27) rising 7.5% / 11.3% / 21.2% / 26.8% across FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27.
- Capital employed (defined as Net Worth + Net Debt) of Rs 1,658 / 1,791 / 2,073 / 2,211 Cr over Q1FY24-Q1FY27, i.e. scale compounding on a broadly flat capital base.
- Working capital days improved 42 / 34 / 28 / 29 (FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27) and fixed asset turnover rose 9.1 / 9.1 / 9.9 / 10.7x, attributed to "Rising salience of asset light business such as Fashion and House of Nykaa".
- No dividend, buyback, debt quantum or fund-raising policy is disclosed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Beauty: 27% GMV growth, 9.6% EBITDA margin; House of Nykaa: 50% GMV growth, 13x growth for Dot & Key; Fashion: 30% GMV growth, turned EBITDA positive at 0.3% in Q4; Superstore: 1,200cr GMV, 500+ bps EBITDA margin improvement
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Deck frames the business as a demand-assortment-distribution flywheel delivering "$2.4 bn Annualized GMV* across all platforms [~3x vs Q1FY24]", with GMV converted at USD 1 = INR 95.
- Assortment moat claimed as "10,000+ Brands across Beauty and Lifestyle" with 160+ new brands launched in Q1 and "~5,300 Brands onboarded in three years"; Beauty+Fashion brand count shown rising 4,992 / 6,683 / 9,067 / 10,275 from Q1FY24 to Q1FY27.
- Content and creator ecosystem positioned as a structural differentiator: "170k+ creators", "2.3mn+ content pieces generated annually", "19 mn+ social media followers", plus Nykaa Play with 300K+ subscribers.
- Consumer base of 60 mn [33% YoY], shown compounding 26 / 35 / 45 / 60 mn over Q1FY24-Q1FY27.
- Fashion described as "India's #1 destination for premium and curated fashion", with Nykaa Fashion operating Nike.in and the Nike App in India.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Nykaa is acquiring a 51% stake in premium dermocosmetic skincare brand Aminu for Rs 32 Crores, with the remaining 49% to be acquired over the next few years per the transaction documents; the deal is expected to close in Q2FY27 subject to regulatory approvals, and the founding team (Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta) continues to run the business.
- [Acquisition rationale] Aminu is disclosed at Rs 19 Cr FY26 net revenue, 8x revenue growth in 3 years, 30+ SKUs, 30+ proprietary formulations and 150+ high-performing ingredients; bootstrapped and profitable since inception, it brings a 'Skin-Intelligence' lab and fills the premium/derma skincare white space in House of Nykaa.
- [Partnership] Nykaa Fashion operates Nike.in and the Nike App in India, with 1.5 mn+ app installs within 6 months of launch; Nike is among the top 3 brands on Nykaa and is live across Nykaa Fashion and Nykaa Man.
- [Regulatory] Part of the Superstore portfolio was impacted by GST-led MRP reductions, "which is expected to normalise over the coming quarters".
- [Recognition] Kay Beauty won "Best New Brand" at the CEW UK Awards within a year of its UK debut at Space NK.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin improved 132 bps to 45.1% due to higher mix of House of Nykaa brands and service income; fulfillment costs up 23 bps (investment in efficiency); marketing/S&D up 10 bps (strategic CAPEX); employee cost and overheads down, driving EBITDA margin to 7.5%
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: sustained mid-20s GMV growth expected; margin: continued EBITDA expansion anticipated across verticals; order inflow: strong brand onboarding (1,200+ new fashion brands, 200+ beauty brands); capex/commissioning: capex at 1% of revenue, focused on beauty retail, fulfillment, and tech
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: House of Nykaa brands scaling to 12+ brands; international expansion (Kay Beauty in UK/GCC); Nykaa Perfumery and experiential retail formats; AI-driven personalization unlocking higher LTV; Superstore as primary D2C distribution channel for emerging brands
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Nykaa delivered record revenue and profitability growth in FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 7.5% and PAT margin hitting 2%, driven by accelerated growth in House of Nykaa brands and profitable turnaround in Fashion; the company is now a dominant omnichannel platform in beauty and fashion with AI-enhanced customer acquisition and brand partnerships like Nike and H&M creating new revenue streams.

open.item: House of Nykaa delivered Rs 3,176 cr GMV FY26 (~50% YoY; beauty Rs 2,788 cr, +65%, 4x in 3 years); growth strategy is three-pronged (scale the 4 breakout brands, push incubating brands past Rs 150 cr, and acquire/build new brands), with confidence in high portfolio growth though not necessarily 65% repeated.

Nykaa Fashion added ~1,200-1,300 brands in FY26 (H&M #1 since launch, plus Nike), expanded emerging categories (men +60%, kids +50%, home +40%) and is leaning heavily into creator-economy content-to-commerce marketing going forward.

Depreciating rupee, high oil prices and inflation could pressure consumption and prompt brand price hikes (not yet passed on); direct imports are a small, fully-hedged (2-3 months) portion, and beauty is a resilient 'small luxury'.

Nykaa Now (30 min-2 hr) network built out to ~75-80 rapid stores across top 7 metros covering 80-90% of relevant pincodes; FY27 plan is to market it aggressively so it contributes a much more meaningful percent of orders.

April/May FY27 growth momentum has been good and management broadly expects to sustain the recent mid-20s growth zone, while staying cautious on macro (currency/oil/inflation) and expecting AI-led benefits on both top line and costs.
Management sees the possibility of double-digit EBITDA margin over the next 3-4 years as growth businesses mature and marketing/S&D costs fall (hedged, not firm guidance).

Beauty retail on track to reach ~500 stores over 3-4 years (guidance given ~2 years ago); FY27 plan ~50-70 new doors (~170-180 more over next 2-3 years), densifying Tier 2/3 towns from a current base of 313 stores in 99 cities.

Nykaa now operates Kiehl's India business (boutiques + kiehls.com + exclusive Nykaa.com retail) and builds/operates Charlotte Tilbury's exclusive brand stores (first in APAC, exclusivity extended 6+ years), a full-stack model it hopes to replicate with more brands.
Committed to generating higher operating cash flows, supported by efficient working capital management and optimisation of capital expenditure.
Pursue steady margin expansion through a disciplined approach to unit economics, leveraging increasing scale and integrating AI into operations to drive operating efficiencies.

Continue to expand the physical retail store footprint while making deliberate investments to acquire new customers, improve order-to-delivery speeds and leverage technology and automation for efficiency.

The Company commits to granular, comprehensive segment-level disclosure for its two core segments - Beauty and Fashion - through quarterly results, quarterly revenue updates and annual disclosures, alongside quarterly earnings calls and an annual Investor Day.

Superstore (eB2B) reached ~Rs 1,200 cr GMV in 4 years with ~0.5M retailers across 1,300 cities and +500bps EBITDA improvement; ~30% of orders now self-serve, continuing scale-led unit economics gains (steady-state single-digit margin business).

Beauty vertical EBITDA at 9.6% FY26 (10.3% Q4, +70bps YoY); each sub-business independently improving margins, but core beauty retail will reinvest efficiency gains into growth, so similar year-over-year margin trajectory can be expected all else equal.
Continue investing in core growth engines while taking a phased approach to investing in new, emerging opportunity areas through organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions.
Nykaa Fashion has managed Nike's India digital commerce (Nike.com + Nike app) end-to-end since February; early signs positive in the first few months of this differentiated (non-marketplace) model.
India-UK and India-EU free trade agreements could lower import duties on beauty/cosmetics, a potential net positive improving brand access and pricing, but not yet quantified and pending detail.
Signed partnerships with YouTube (integrating shopping into videos) and Snapchat (nurturing next-gen Gen Z beauty creators), leveraging Nykaa's 100,000+ influencer affiliate network.
Board approved acquiring the remaining 40% stake in nutricosmetics brand Nudge for Rs 14.2 lakh, taking Nykaa to 100% to sharpen focus on health and wellness.
Board approved acquiring an additional 39% stake in Dot & Key (taking Nykaa to 90%) for Rs 265 cr; brand at ~Rs 750 cr annualized GMV run rate and profitable since Q4CY23.

verdicts.item: Physical retail at 187 stores across 68 cities (GMV +50% 3yr, EBITDA +105%); rolling out larger, more impactful flagship stores (first at Linking Road) with more to come in coming months and years.
verdicts.note: 'we have more than doubled our retail footprint over the past 3 years' with multiple new experiential/flagship formats - continued rollout of larger/differentiated stores.

verdicts.item: Owned brand Dot & Key hit ~Rs 580 cr+ annualized GMV in Q4FY24 and, on March momentum, is likely to annualize to Rs 700 cr+; profitable since Jan-2023 with offline distribution being added.
verdicts.note: 'This brand grew enormously in the last 3 years at 13x, delivering INR 1,790 crores of GMV' - far exceeding the Rs 700 cr+ expectation. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Capex is significantly lower in FY24 vs FY23 as office and warehouse investment is largely complete; company will continue to invest in retail expansion and tech capabilities.
verdicts.note: 'Our capex utilization... currently stands at about 1% of revenue... We continue to invest in beauty retail store expansion, fulfilment capabilities as well as technology' - low-capex, retail/tech-inv…

verdicts.item: By September 2024, ~70-80% of orders from the top 12 metros and ~50% of orders from the next ~110 cities to be fulfilled same-day/next-day, taking ~50% of all India orders to same/next-day delivery.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 6Q past horizon Q2FY25

verdicts.item: The elevated-discounting cycle that widened the GMV vs Net Revenue gap is at its end; from here GMV and Net Revenue growth are expected to be similar.
verdicts.note: Record gross margin and net-revenue growth confirm the discounting cycle ended and GMV/NSV growth converged.

verdicts.item: Board approved acquiring a majority stake in D2C clean-beauty brand Earth Rhythm (making it a subsidiary); Q1FY25 GMV ~Rs 55 cr, grown 8x over 3 years off a small base.
verdicts.note: 'We had acquired 76% stake in Earth Rhythm... and we now completed the acquisition by acquiring an additional 24% stake' - majority stake taken and fully completed.

verdicts.item: Prestige fragrance market share reached ~13% in FY24 (+300bps YoY) and is expected to keep improving in FY25 as fragrance becomes the third core beauty pillar.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Superstore (eB2B) grew 72% YoY with contribution margin +520bps and is on its journey toward breakeven per the long-term plan.
verdicts.note: 'because of our growing scale... we have improved our EBITDA margin by greater than 500 bps' - breakeven journey continuing but not yet reached.

verdicts.item: Within the Beauty vertical, the most meaningful margin improvement is expected to come from the eB2B (Superstore) business scaling, while beauty.com/retail margins stay healthy and owned brands grow faster than the platform.
verdicts.note: 'each business is independently seeing improvement in their margin profile' with eB2B improving and owned brands outpacing - Beauty-vertical margin-mix improvement as described.

verdicts.item: Services (ad) income and demand expected to strengthen in H2FY25 (festive season) as D2C brands return to advertising and discounting moderates on demand revival, aiding BPC gross margins.
verdicts.note: 'gross margin improving by 132 basis points in FY '26, led by strong performance of House of Nykaa and improved service income across businesses' - services/ad income strengthened as expected.

verdicts.item: Management retains Investor Day guidance to break even in the Fashion vertical at EBITDA level during FY26; Q1 EBITDA improved to -6.2% (+304bps YoY).
verdicts.note: 'we reported a positive 30 basis points EBITDA for the fourth quarter' and 'Fashion has become profitable' - FY26 breakeven guidance delivered.

verdicts.item: Fashion grew 25% GMV, above market, and management believes it will sustainably and comfortably outstrip market growth in the coming quarters as a structural improvement.
verdicts.note: 'the financial year '26 was 30% growth, almost reaching INR 5,000 crores in GMV' with an accelerating exit - sustained above-market growth as claimed.

wtt.summary: 75% guidance hit (14 chains); 5/6 projects on-time; 2 expired; 18% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident, framing FY26 as a record year of profitable growth with 14 quarters of sustained mid-20s growth; management stayed disciplined on not giving hard forward numbers, flagged macro/currency/inflation caution, and repeatedly stressed reinvesting margin gains back into growth.

meta.thesis: Nykaa delivered record revenue and profitability growth in FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 7.5% and PAT margin hitting 2%, driven by accelerated growth in House of Nykaa brands and profitable turnaround in Fashion; the company is now a dominant omnichannel platform in beauty and fashion with AI-enhanced customer acquisition and brand partnerships like Nike and H&M creating new revenue streams.
